issues.failure_explanation: The paper works throughout in P_2 (finite second moments only) and cites central limit theorems to justify passing from the mean-field theory to ensembles. A bound E||Sigma_hat - Sigma||_F ~ N^{-1/2} for sample covariances needs roughly finite fourth moments, because the entries of Sigma_hat are averages of products. For laws in P_2 with infinite fourth moment the expected error can decay more slowly, or the expectation can fail to be controlled. The stated rate therefore does not hold in the setting the paper defines.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the rate under an explicit extra assumption (e.g. finite fourth moments) or say only that Sigma_hat converges to Sigma almost surely for pi in P_2.
issues.overall_effect: The heuristic link between the mean-field results and finite-N behaviour, including the expected parametric error decay in the experiments, is stated for a class of laws where it is not justified. No formal theorem depends on it.
issues.title: N^{-1/2} covariance-error rate asserted under only finite second moments
issues.why_classification: A one-line added hypothesis or rewording fixes the sentence. None of the formal results or the exactness analysis is affected.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper argues that S_dec is non-generic because the equation phi_U(t)=phi_U(lambda t)phi_{U_lambda}(t) is 'unsatisfiable' for characteristic functions with zeros, naming the uniform law. This is false. If U is uniform on [0,1] and B is an independent Bernoulli(1/2) variable, then U equals in law U'/2 + B/2 (binary expansion), so U is 1/2-decomposable. Since lambda is existentially quantified in S_dec, a uniform Z paired with a Bernoulli Y (w=1/2, lambda=1/2) satisfies the S_dec identity. The cited mechanism (a zero of phi_U) does not by itself rule out decomposability.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete or correct the example, e.g. replace it by a statement that decomposability fails for a specific lambda, or drop the uniform and atom examples. The theorems are untouched.
issues.overall_effect: The informal justification that S_dec is small or non-generic is partly wrong, and the stated illustrations of laws outside S_dec are incorrect. Theorem thm:enkf_update_unique itself is unaffected.
issues.title: False example: uniform law is claimed not to be lambda-decomposable
issues.why_classification: It is a local correction to heuristic motivation. The rigorous results and their proofs are not involved.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem thm:F_char only shows F \ E^EnKU is contained in S_nl-dec, and S_nl-dec is defined as the subset of F satisfying a decomposition identity. No size measure for S_nl-dec is ever given, yet the paper concludes 'narrow', 'no headroom' and 'near-optimal'. The class is not small in any evident sense. Take n=m=1, any pi_Y, any measurable non-affine d with d(Y) in L^2, and lambda in (0,1). Let Z = sum_{k>=0} lambda^{k+1}(d(Y^(k)) - E d(Y)) and X = Z + d(Y). Then L(x,y)=lambda x + d(y_star) - lambda E d(Y) is weakly y_star-dependent and exact. Moreover pi satisfies the S_nl-dec identity (v=1, w=0, u=lambda), and pi is not in E^EnKU because translation families determine d up to an affine term. So S_nl-dec contains a family indexed by arbitrary nonlinear d and arbitrary pi_Y. Separately, F is a union over all L, not the exact set of any single map, so the sentence calling F the maximal exact set of a single update is inaccurate. What is proved is only the inclusion E(L) ⊆ E^EnKU ∪ S_nl-dec for each weakly y_star-dependent L.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the conclusion as the inclusion E(L) ⊆ E^EnKU ∪ S_nl-dec for every weakly y_star-dependent L, and drop 'narrow', 'maximal exact set of a single update' and 'near-optimal' unless a precise smallness statement for S_nl-dec is proved. Optionally mention the explicit nonlinear-shift family as a non-negligible exception.
issues.overall_effect: The headline interpretation (abstract, Section 3 and Discussion) that the EnKU is near-optimal among weakly y_star-dependent affine maps and that there is essentially no headroom beyond it is not supported. Theorem thm:F_char as a set identity remains true but carries much less information than advertised.
issues.title: Near-optimality of the EnKU rests on an unquantified 'narrow' class S_nl-dec that contains a family indexed by arbitrary nonlinear shifts
issues.why_classification: The formal theorem and proofs survive. The repair is a contained weakening or reformulation of the advertised conclusion and the corresponding prose, with no new proof architecture. It does remove a central selling point, hence more than minor.
